differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.
Balcony and pedestal carving, Ionic volute sections and stair-head scrolls are schematic rather than the photographed profiles.
Granite courses and rock-face variation remain too regular; the checker stones and upper capital/head-band profiles need further photographic refinement.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
The earlier low stone boundary replaces the generic iron fence with urns. Its exact post/rail sections remain reconstructed.

T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.
T-2564: the corner pinnacle caps are ogival with a moulded collar and ball finial, and the front coping sweeps up into each.
A brown cornice-box band shows under the lattice where the photograph shows stone (T-2566).
Whether the stone parapet continues at full height behind the rear pinnacle, or drops there to the brick, is not resolved by this picture; the model drops it.
